what: The board (background color plus large text on top) is baked into a single image and laid over a WebGL fluid. Wherever the mouse passes, the fluid dye melts it transparent and cuts a hole. Through the holes the video and photos behind the board show. On a 256² velocity grid and a 512² dye grid, dye is splatted with trail radius 6e-5 and force 5900. Each frame velocity decays by .962 and dye by .988, and 20 pressure iterations even out the flow. Wherever dye × 3.9 exceeds .5 (an edge .01 wide), it is cut open. The further the board scrolls up off screen (the share that has passed above relative to board height, squared), the weaker the splat force and the faster (.97) the trails fade

options.force: Force mouse movement gives the flow, default 5900
options.fade: Share of dye kept each frame, default .988 (.97 near scroll end)
options.flow: Share of speed kept each frame, default .962
options.[data-fx-part=ink]: (If present) text to bake into the plate too — single-line text or several characters. After baking, the on-screen text is hidden

note: three must be global (window.THREE) for this to run — if it is missing the panel stays as it is (no damage). What shows behind the panel (the video) must be laid beneath it so the punched-out spot is not empty. On touch devices it is punched through by dragging (not blocked). When the panel size changes it is baked again
